subject: pe
title: Drive Theory and Inverted-U
welcome_lead: From linear performance to peak-and-decline — two classic arousal theories.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on drive theory and the inverted-U hypothesis.
final_note: Beginners need calm; experts can ride higher arousal — task complexity changes the curve.

concepts.def: Performance = Habit × Drive; rises linearly with arousal (Hull).
Yerkes-Dodson: performance peaks at moderate arousal.
Strongest habit triggered under arousal; correct for experts, often wrong for novices.
Activation level of the autonomic nervous system.
Complex tasks show inverted-U at lower arousal optimum.
Optimal arousal depends on task difficulty.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hull's theory predicts performance rises with arousal — supported only when dominant response is correct.
Original mice experiments showed optimal arousal at moderate stress; performance falls at extremes.
Snooker peak at low arousal; rugby tackling at higher. Complexity shifts the optimum down.
